# Training Lens · 训练视窗
A local, read-only training dashboard for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**. Turn existing TensorBoard scal
ar logs into a focused view of progress and trends, without changing your trainer.
简体中文 · DSH plugin documentation
Screenshot uses generated demonstration data, not a training result.
## Features
- Choose any primary and secondary scalar: reward, validation loss, accuracy, learning rate, or a cu

stom tag.
- Explicit **higher / lower is better** selection. By default, show the observed range wit

hout declaring improvement.
- Raw values, optional EMA smoothing, per-metric steps and expandable di

agnostics.
- Chinese / English UI, responsive layout, automatic refresh and run selection.
- DSH too
l starts, inspects and stops only its own dashboard. No trainer controls, telemetry or cloud upload.
- Works even when the TensorBoard web server is not running. No browser extension, front-end build
en the TensorBoard web server is not running. No browser extension, front-end build or CDN required.

side the declared DSH 0.2 range is not assumed.

p` if needed. For local testing: `dsh plugin --profile lens-test add /absolute/path/to/dsh-training-
r local testing: `dsh plugin --profile lens-test add /absolute/path/to/dsh-training-lens-0.1.0.tgz`.
The Python helper uses your existing training environment. If TensorBoard is missing, install the op

The plugin never runs pip automatically. npm registry publication is separate from these GitHub inst
allation methods; do not assume `npm install dsh-training-lens` is available until an npm release ex

## Use in DSH
Ask DSH:
> Use training_lens to open my TensorBoard logs at `/absolute/path/to/runs`, using Python `/absolute
/path/to/venv/bin/python`.
On Windows, provide the training environment's `...\.venv\Scripts\python.exe`. The tool returns a lo
cal URL; open it to choose a run and metrics.
Tool parameters:
| Field | Meaning |

| `action` | `start`, `status`, or `stop` |
| `logdir` | Absolute event directory or parent director

y of runs |
| `python` | Existing Python executable, not a shell command |
| `port` | `0` chooses a
free port; an occupied fixed port fails without stopping its owner |
The process remains tied to the plugin instance. Disabling/reloading the plugin or closing DSH stops
its dashboard. Stopping the dashboard leaves the training process and event files untouched. Only o
ne dashboard is owned by a plugin instance; stop it before changing the root/interpreter.

## Interpretation and limits
- Status means recent **scalar timestamps**, not trainer liveness. A completed target is not proof o

f successful training or saved checkpoints.
- Standard TensorBoard scalar and TF2 scalar-plugin tens
or summaries are supported. Unknown tags are selectable; success rate is never inferred from reward.
- The default x-axis is the writer's step. Known MCTS tag combinations may expose epoch progress fr

om numeric `training_epochs` in `config.yaml`; generic `Train/loss` is not assumed to use epochs.
-
Metrics may be logged at different frequencies. The card and point tooltip identify the metric's own

step.
- NaN and Infinity are gaps, not zeros. Duplicate steps use the newest event after TensorBoar

d's restart-purge behavior.
- Charts above 1,600 points retain bucket endpoints/extrema/gap markers.

Cards use the full parsed series; EMA is applied to displayed points.
- Event readers are cached fo
r up to four runs. Very large mixed-media event files can use substantial memory. Use a focused log

root.
- Hidden/cache/checkpoint directories and symlink entries are skipped. No arbitrary-file HTTP
endpoint exists. Only loopback hosts are accepted; this is not an authenticated remote hosting servi

ce.
- In remote DSH environments the URL refers to the DSH host. Use your normal SSH/editor port for
warding; the plugin does not open a public tunnel.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Set `TRAINING_LENS_TEST_PYTHON` to a Python executable with TensorBoard to enable the Node end-to-en
d lifecycle test. Python integration tests explicitly skip if optional dependencies are unavailable;
CI installs them. No real training is run in tests. `npm pack` contains an allowlisted set of sourc
e/assets/docs, with no install lifecycle scripts.

they are installed separately rather than vendored.
